conventions.edgeReading: edges[i] = { proofOrEvidence, requires, ownedBy } means: the proof or evidence named by 'proofOrEvidence' REQUIRES the fact/evidence named by 'requires'; 'ownedBy' names the single aggregate (or immutable creation authority) that owns and linearizes the REQUIRED fact (one fact, one owner, one linearization point).
conventions.terminalProofIds: TerminalProof:<scope>.<kind> with scope in {cell, workplace, node, process, stage, lifecycle, run} and kind in {success, failure, cancellation, unreachable}. 'failure' means truthful failure.
conventions.scopeLadder: cell (production-cell accepted-material chain, owner Workplace) < workplace (author/reviewer/repair loop, owner Workplace) < node (dependency-graph work scope, owner NodeRun) < process (owner ProcessRun) < stage (owner StageRun) < lifecycle (owner LifecycleRun) < run (owner FactoryRun). The containment ladder is taken from the WP-03 scope list plus the target-model relation set; the plan text itself does not freeze the fan-in member of each settlement scope (gap G7).
conventions.eventCoRequisite: Every required fact commits in one transaction with its exact WorkflowEvent naming source owner, source revision, transition kind and evidence refs (plan 'Durable handoff'; target-model WorkflowEvent row). This co-requisite applies to every edge and is not exploded into a separate edge per fact; WorkflowEvent appears as a node only where the event/command itself is the load-bearing evidence (operator stop, obligation creation).

ownedBySpecials.Planning: single immutable creation command authority for WorkItem/WorkItemDependency/planning-claim facts (immutable planning facts; no mutable board status)
ownedBySpecials.InstalledWorkshopManifest: immutable content-addressed workshop semantics (CheckPlans, CanonicalRoleContract, PromptBudgetProfile, effect contracts); not a mutable aggregate owner
ownedBySpecials.TargetOwnerCapability: the stateless obligation consumer acting for the exact target aggregate named by the obligation; obligations and their completion receipts are durable kernel-ledger rows whose completion commits only in the target fact's transaction
ownedBySpecials.OwningScopeAggregate: the aggregate whose scope owns the wait (Workplace, NodeRun, ProcessRun, StageRun, LifecycleRun, FactoryRun, or ActivityAttempt for attempt-scoped waits)
ownedBySpecials.CommandedScopeAggregate: the aggregate addressed by the operator command; stop/resume are durable commands and evidence, never direct state updates

conventions.physicalNames: All names are logical. Physical names are frozen by EK-1; renaming during freeze does not change this graph's typed node/edge sets.
conventions.quantifiers: Unquantified edges are per-instance. Where a proof requires 'every member/effect/gate', the note says so; reconciliation should treat such edges as the typed edge plus the universal quantifier recorded in 'quantifier'.

gaps.underspecification: The plan freezes the truthful-failure proof kind and its sources (gate terminal reject, effect policy terminal) but never freezes the evidence predicate that distinguishes 'another repair transition is lawful' from 'no lawful repair remains' (repair-budget/policy exhaustion evidence kind unnamed). The backward closure therefore stops at the rejecting decision without a proving 'terminality' fact.

No in-run evidence predicate for run-scope unreachability is stated anywhere. Ingress/protocol refusals (capsule corrupt, foreign lineage, FACTORY_DATABASE_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED) occur before run start, and the unreachable semantics of 'Durable handoff' are written for dependants of a terminally failed predecessor, not for the run scope itself. Edges are best-effort and flagged.

The plan requires typed waits for human input, external availability, policy and quota 'with exact wake sources', and the human-input discharge is clearly a typed command translated from the operator UI; the discharge evidence KINDS for external-availability and policy/quota wakes are not named (external availability event receipt? quota-release receipt?).

A crash after an un-idempotent external send becomes 'typed uncertainty, never a blind duplicate send', but the evidence that RESOLVES the uncertainty (idempotency probe receipt, external confirmation receipt, human disposition) is not named; the backward closure from an effect-terminal proof through an unknown effect is open.

The target model gives one line ('Exact cell completion evidence') and ADR-053 gives the AcceptedCandidateAuthority field set for the effect input, but whether CellFinalAcceptance itself must embed acceptanceDigest and materialDigest/semanticDigest equality with the accepted WorkplaceProductionRevision (vs only gate+effect refs) is not frozen. EK-1 must freeze the field set; the edge set here may grow by digest-equality edges.

Stop/resume are durable commands and evidence, and outer-scope cancellation proofs are derived, but the plan does not state whether an outer-scope cancellation proof requires per-member TerminalProof:cancellation references or one proof naming member dispositions; nor how in-flight ActivityAttempt leases across all scopes are proven dispositioned. The TypedWaitDisposition quantifier at run scope is an inference.

The target model names LifecycleRun/StageRun/ProcessRun/NodeRun and EK-6 requires settlement proofs for 'Node, Process, Stage and Lifecycle', but the plan text never freezes which members each scope fans in over (workplaces-per-node, nodes-per-process, processes-per-stage, stages-per-lifecycle). The ladder used here follows the WP-03 scope list and the ADR-053 obligation chain (FinalAcceptance -> SettleProcess -> RouteLifecycle); stage-level edges are pattern-inferred.

'Every terminal lifecycle claim has an owned construction surface and an executable verifier' fixes existence, but the receipt kind a verifier produces (and whether a CheckPlan instance is per-cell manifest content or per-decision instance evidence owned elsewhere) is not frozen; ownedBy for these nodes may move at EK-1 without changing the topology.
